newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast power stable despite oil, gas rise.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast power stable despite oil, gas rise.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. were stable Friday despite rallies in the oil and natural gas markets on forecast of a cold snap in the eastern U.S. next week.
"A lot of utilities are avoiding burning oil and gas if possible," said a New York trader.
Swing New York City gate natgas was quoted at $4.10 per million British thermal unit, up slightly from Thursday.

On the New York Merchantile Exchange, January natural gas futures with delivery at the Henry Hub offshore Louisiana closed up 32.9 cents at $3.855. January futures for crude at Cushing, Okla., ended up 72 cents at $24.44 a barrel

The 800 megawatt (MW) Fitzpatrick nuclear power plant in Scriba, N.Y., was expected be fully back early next following its refueling outage, and the 1,000 MW fossil fuel-fired Ravenswood unit 3 in Long Island City, N.Y., was planned to resume operation Monday.

In the New York Power Pool (NYPP), peak, non-firm electricity in the western portion of the grid for Saturday was quoted near $18.00, Sunday $17.00 and Monday $23.00 a megawatt hour (MWh). Today's quotes compared with Thursday's $22.50-$23.50 for Friday.
Western NYPP non-firm power for delivery Saturday was notational pegged near $15.50, Sunday $15.00 and Monday $16.00, compared with Thursday's $14.50-$15.00.
In eastern NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity for Saturday was valued near 24.00, Sunday $23.00 and Monday $29.00-$30.00. Today's quotes compared with $29.00 Thursday.

Non-firm deliveries in eastern NYPP during light load periods on Saturday were talked near $24.00, Sunday $23.00 and Monday $19.00-$20.00. Today's assessments compared with Thursday's $19.00-$20.00 for Friday.
Short-term power values in New England remained firm as the unplanned outage of the 910 MW Maine Yankee nuclear power plant will continue through the weekend.

The operator Maine Yankee Atomic Power Co today announced the Wiscasset, Maine, generating station would return on line next week after complete review of cable systems. The plant was shut December 6 after engineers found a couple of calbes to the plant's main control room had been improperly routed.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Monday at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border was quoted at $35.00-$36.00/MWh, up from Thursday's $34.00-$35.00 for Friday.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Monday delivery to the NU border was steady at $20.00-$21.00.
For the balance of December, peak, non-firm power at the NU power was valued near $34.00, higher than $33.00 Thursday, and off-peak, non-firm power near $20.00, up from Thursday's $16.00-$17.00.
